title: The Uncountable Larder
intro: Un consejo, una información — perfectly countable in Spanish. Advice, information — stubbornly, permanently singular in English. Stock the larder correctly.

A2.why: Spanish “un consejo” is countable; English says “a piece of advice” or “some advice”.
“Muebles” is plural, but furniture is one mass: “The furniture is new.”
Count the bags, not the luggage: “three bags” or “three pieces of luggage”.
Spanish has “informaciones”; English only has “information” or “a piece of information”.
Money takes a singular verb: “The money is on the table.”

A2.right: reports of recent events — always takes a singular verb
A2.why: News ends in -s but is singular: “The news is good”, “a piece of news”.

A2.right: tasks a teacher sets to do at home
A2.why: “Deberes” is plural, but homework is uncountable: “I have a lot of homework.”
Bread is a mass: “some bread”, “a loaf of bread” or “a slice of bread”.
Liquids are uncountable: “some milk”, “a glass of milk”.
Rice is a mass of tiny grains: “The rice for the paella is ready.”
Count the songs, not the music: “a piece of music”, “three songs”.

A2.right: what grows on your head — takes a singular verb
A2.why: Spanish “el pelo” is singular too: “Her hair is grey.” “A hair” is one single strand.

B1.why: Traffic is one mass of cars: “There was a lot of traffic on the way to Valencia.”

B1.right: tools or machines for a job
B1.why: Say “a piece of equipment”, never “an equipment”.
As a noun, progress is uncountable: “The patient is making good progress”, never “a progress” or “progresses”.
No “a” with weather: “What lovely weather!”, not “What a lovely weather!”
Say “a piece of research” or “a study”, never “a research”.
Knowledge has no plural, though “a good knowledge of Spanish” is fine.

B1.right: a place to live or stay
B1.why: In British English it is uncountable: “We found accommodation in Ruzafa.”
Scenery is the whole view: “The scenery around the Albufera is beautiful.”
Luck has no plural and no “a luck”: “Good luck!”, “a bit of luck”, “a stroke of luck”.
Fun is uncountable: “We had a lot of fun at the Fallas.”
Ask for permission, not “a permission”: Spanish “un permiso” is the trap.
Damage has no plural for harm; “damages” is money a court orders you to pay.

B2.right: comments on how well something was done
B2.why: Feedback is uncountable: “some feedback”, “a piece of feedback”.
Count the programs, not the software: “a piece of software”, “two apps”.
Say “a piece of evidence”; Spanish “evidencias” is the trap.
Machinery is the mass; one is “a machine” or “a piece of machinery”.
Poetry is the art; a single text is “a poem”.

B2.right: cleaning, ironing and other jobs at home
B2.why: Housework is uncountable: “I do the housework on Saturdays”, never “houseworks”.
Jewellery is the collection; one item is “a piece of jewellery”, or name it: a ring.
Cutlery is uncountable: “Put the cutlery on the table.”
Rubbish is uncountable in British English: “Take the rubbish out.”
Livestock is the whole herd: “The ranch’s livestock was sold at auction.”
Say “a round of applause”, never “an applause”.
Clothing is uncountable, clothes is plural; one thing is “an item of clothing”.

C1.why: Expertise is uncountable: “her expertise in surgery”, never “her expertises”.

C1.right: understanding something only after it has happened
C1.why: Hindsight is uncountable: “With hindsight, we should have left earlier.”
Legislation is the body of laws; one is “a law” or “a piece of legislation”.
Footage is uncountable: “some footage”; one short piece is “a clip”.
All the letters together: “His correspondence was published after his death.”
Merchandise is the goods as a whole; one thing is “an item” or “a product”.
Foliage is all the leaves together; one is simply “a leaf”.
Stationery with -ery is the supplies; “stationary” with -ary means not moving.
“The cowboy ran out of ammunition”, never “ran out of ammunitions”.

C1.right: wild animals and plants in their habitat
C1.why: Wildlife is uncountable: “The Albufera’s wildlife is rich.”

C1.right: all the bits and pieces linked to an activity
C1.why: A mass noun: “all the paraphernalia of a country doctor’s bag”.
Hospitality is uncountable: “Thank you for your hospitality.”
